## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

---
# fmt: skip file
title: Directives
description: Tell Yamark what to format, skip, preserve, or configure from inside the file.
---

<!-- fmt: skip file -->

The source file is the primary interface. Put a small `fmt:` directive next to
the text it controls, then let an editor or repository integration run Yamark.
Because directives are comments, the formatting choice stays with the text.
The comment marker depends on the file:

| File | Directive comment |
| --- | --- |
| Markdown and Quarto | `<!-- fmt: ... -->` |
| YAML, Python, and R | `# fmt: ...` |

Quarto chunk options use `#|`; for example, `#| fmt: skip`.

## Target the next value or block

Most directives apply to the next supported target. In a YAML file, that target
is usually a scalar node. In a Python or R file, it is usually a string literal
or a contiguous source-comment block. The directive does not format the
surrounding Python or R source code.

## YAML files

Mark a scalar as Markdown and choose sentence wrapping for that scalar:

```yaml
# fmt: markdown wrap=sentence
description: "Explain the project in a few clear sentences."
other_value: "This is ordinary YAML, not Markdown."
```

The directive attaches to `description`, the next scalar. A tagged scalar is
another way to mark Markdown when the setting should travel with the value:

```yaml
instructions: !markdown |
  # Review

  Read the diff and report concrete correctness issues.
```

Use the same placement for an embedded formatter. The formatter name is the
language after `fmt:`:

```yaml
# fmt: python
script: |
  def check(items):return all(item > 0 for item in items)
```

YAML also supports directives on a collection parent when the setting describes
the collection rather than a scalar:

```yaml
# fmt: table
- {name: alpha, type: string, default: ""}
- {name: beta, type: integer, default: 0}
```

## Python files

Put `# fmt: markdown` immediately before the string literal or comment block
that contains Markdown:

```python
# fmt: markdown wrap=sentence
REVIEW_PROMPT = """
# Review

Read the diff and report concrete correctness issues. Prefer specific examples.
"""
```

The `#` lines inside the string are Markdown content. Python outside the
marked target is left for a Python formatter such as Ruff.

The same directive can target a Markdown comment block:

```python
# fmt: markdown
# # Filters
#
# Apply the most specific filter first.
#
# - Each filter is a single expression.
```

For a non-Markdown embedded language, use its formatter name:

```python
# fmt: r
analysis = """
f <- function(x) x + 1
"""
```

## R files

R uses the same `# fmt:` marker. It can target a raw string literal used for a
vignette, help text, or a Shiny message:

```r
# fmt: markdown wrap=sentence
help_text <- r"(
# Filters

Apply the most specific filter first. Explain why a filter matched.
)"
```

It can also target a contiguous Markdown comment block:

```r
# fmt: markdown
# # Filters
#
# Apply the most specific filter first.
#
# - Each filter is a single expression.
```

For source code inside a YAML literal scalar, use the language formatter name
in the same way as in a YAML file:

```yaml
# fmt: r
analysis: |
  f <- function(x)x+1
```

## Control a region or a whole file

The scope is part of the directive. `next` is the default for target directives.
Use `from-here` for the rest of a region, and `file` for a document-wide
------
#| name: demo
#| launcher:
#|   vanilla: true
#|   default-packages: [base, utils]

main <- function() NULL
```

without changing the surrounding Python. Add `# fmt: markdown` before the

:::: {.showcase-before-after}

# Data Visualization

A chart is **read by people and executed by you**. This skill turns "make it look
good" into a procedure with checks, so the result is right by construction rather
than by taste.

**The method here is design-system-agnostic.** Nothing in the procedure, the form
heuristic, the six checks, or the mark specs is specific to one product. A design
system supplies a small set of *parameters* (its ramps, a categorical order, a
diverging pair, a status palette, a texture, its surfaces, its filter components);
the method consumes them unchanged. A **validated default palette** is the
reference instance, fully specified in `references/palette.md`. To target your
brand, read that file's structure and substitute its values - touch nothing else.

> The single most important habit: **the color part is computable, so compute it.**
> Never eyeball whether a palette is colorblind-safe - run `scripts/validate_palette.js`.

## The procedure - do these in order

Color comes LAST. Most bad charts pick colors first.

1. **Pick the form.** What is the data's job - magnitude, identity, polarity, a
   single headline, change-over-time? The job picks the chart type, and sometimes
   the answer is *not a chart* (a stat tile or hero number). -> `references/choosing-a-form.md`
2. **Assign color by the job it does.** Categorical (identity), sequential
   (magnitude), diverging (polarity), or status (state) - each has one rule.
   Assign categorical hues in fixed order, never cycled. -> `references/color-formula.md`
3. **VALIDATE the palette - run the script, don't reason about Delta E.**
   `node scripts/validate_palette.js "<hex,hex,...>" --mode light` (relative to
   this skill's base directory - or load it as `<script type="module">` in the
   chart's own page, where it reads
   `data-palette` off `<body>` and logs a `console.table` report). It returns
   pass/fail on the lightness band, chroma floor, adjacent-pair CVD separation,
   the normal-vision floor, and contrast. Fix anything that FAILs before continuing. Re-run for
   `--mode dark` with that mode's surface.
4. **Apply mark specs & spacers.** Thin marks, 4px rounded data-ends anchored to
   the baseline, 2px lines, >=8px markers, a 2px surface gap between fills (stacked
   segments and adjacent bars alike) and a 2px surface ring on overlapping marks,
   selective direct labels. -> `references/marks-and-anatomy.md`
5. **Add the hover layer - by default.** An HTML/SVG chart *is* interactive; ship
   a crosshair+tooltip on line/area and a per-mark hover tooltip on bar/dot/cell.
   The only form that skips it is a bare stat tile with no plot. Hit targets bigger
   than the mark; filters in one row above the charts. -> `references/interaction.md`
6. **Final accessibility pass.** For >= 2 series a legend is always present and <= 4
   are also direct-labeled (a single series needs no legend box - the title names
   it), so identity is never color-alone; a table view exists; dark mode is **selected** - its own
   steps from the same ramps, validated against the dark surface, not an automatic
   flip; texture is available for the CVD/print/forced-colors case.
7. **Render it and look at it.** The validator checks color, not layout - open or
   screenshot the output and eyeball it for label collisions, geometry, and overflow
   before calling it done.

Then check the result against **`references/anti-patterns.md`** - it is the catalog
of what goes wrong. If your chart matches an entry, it's wrong.

## Non-negotiables (true in every design system)

- **Assign categorical hues in fixed order, never cycled.** A 9th series is never a
  generated hue - it folds into "Other," small multiples, or composite encoding.
- **One axis.** Never a dual-axis chart (two y-scales). Two measures of different
  scale -> two charts, small multiples, or indexed to a common base. *(This is the
  #1 chart mistake - see anti-patterns.)*
- **Color follows the entity, never its rank.** A filter that changes the series
  count must not repaint the survivors.
- **Sequential = one hue, light->dark. Diverging = two hues + a neutral gray
  midpoint.** Never a rainbow; never a hue at the diverging midpoint.
- **Run the validator before shipping any categorical palette.** CVD Delta E >= 8 is the
  target (OKLab ×100); 6-8 is a floor that is legal ONLY with secondary encoding. A
  normal-vision floor below 15 is a hard FAIL - full-color readers can't tell the
  pair apart; re-step it on the adjacent pairlist (secondary encoding does not excuse
  this one); under `--pairs all` cut series or facet instead - see check 4. A contrast WARN
  obligates visible labels or a table view - it is not dismissable.
- **Thin marks; a legend always present for >= 2 series (none for one), with
  selective direct labels (never a number on every point); recessive grid/axes.**
- **Text wears text tokens, never the series color** - values, labels, and legends
  stay in primary/secondary/muted ink; a colored mark beside them carries identity.
- **Status colors are reserved** (good/warning/serious/critical) and never reused
  for "series 4"; they ship with an icon + label, never color alone.

## Plugging in a design system

The method is invariant; only these parameters change per system. The reference
instance - every value filled in - is `references/palette.md`.

| Parameter | What the system provides |
|---|---|
| **Ramps** | the hue scales (named steps) the palette draws from |
| **Categorical theme** | the fixed hue order (a named theme); default + alternates |
| **Sequential hue** | the default single hue for magnitude |
| **Diverging pair** | two warm/cool poles + a neutral midpoint |
| **Status palette** | good / warning / serious / critical - steps distinct from categorical |
| **Texture fill** | one directional hand-drawn fill, used at 45° / 135° |
| **Surfaces** | light & dark chart-surface colors (the validator needs these) |
| **Filter controls** | date-range & dimension controls (behavioral spec in `interaction.md`) |

To onboard a new system: fill those rows, feed its ramps to the validator, and let
it snap each slot to the nearest passing step. Structure and rules stay as written.

## Reference files

| File | What it answers |
|------|-----------------|
| `references/choosing-a-form.md` | Which chart type / is it even a chart? |
| `references/color-formula.md` | The four jobs, the six checks, snap-to-passing |
| `references/marks-and-anatomy.md` | Mark specs, spacers, labels, figures, hero number |
| `references/interaction.md` | Tooltips & hover, filters & time ranges |
| `references/components.md` | The pieces a chart is made of - build each in plain HTML |
| `references/anti-patterns.md` | **What goes wrong - check every chart against this** |
| `references/palette.md` | **The reference palette instance** - every parameter, filled in; swap for your brand's |
| `scripts/validate_palette.js` | Runnable six-checks validator (run it; don't eyeball) |

# Provision the shared analysis servers of the Computational Ecology Lab.
#
# Installs R from the CRAN apt repository, RStudio Server and a Miniforge-based
# Python stack, then creates the lab user accounts.
#
# Usage:
#   ansible-playbook -i inventories/lab.ini ansible_playbook.yml --ask-become-pass
#   ansible-playbook -i inventories/lab.ini ansible_playbook.yml --tags r_packages
#
# Maintainer: Lena Müller <l.mueller@ecolab.example.edu>

- name: Provision shared analysis servers
  hosts: analysis_servers
  become: true
  gather_facts: true

  vars:
    r_version: "4.4.2"
    rstudio_server_version: "2024.12.0-467"
    miniforge_prefix: /opt/miniforge3
    conda_env_name: ecolab-py312
    lab_group: ecolab
    lab_users:
      - { name: amartin, uid: 2101, shell: /bin/bash, admin: true }
      - { name: jchen, uid: 2102, shell: /bin/zsh, admin: false }
      - { name: nokafor, uid: 2103, shell: /bin/bash, admin: false }
      - { name: lmueller, uid: 2104, shell: /bin/bash, admin: true }
    # Binary packages for Ubuntu from Posit Public Package Manager; much faster
    # than compiling the geospatial stack from source after every R upgrade.
    cran_repo: "https://packagemanager.posit.co/cran/__linux__/{{ ansible_distribution_release }}/latest"
    r_packages: [tidyverse, lme4, glmmTMB, brms, targets, renv, devtools, rmarkdown, sf, terra, unmarked]
    apt_defaults: &apt_defaults
      update_cache: true
      cache_valid_time: 3600
      state: present

  pre_tasks:
    - name: Fail early on unsupported distributions
      ansible.builtin.assert:
        that:
          - ansible_distribution == "Ubuntu"
          - ansible_distribution_version is version("22.04", ">=")
        fail_msg: >-
          This playbook only supports Ubuntu 22.04 or newer, but
          {{ inventory_hostname }} runs {{ ansible_distribution }}
          {{ ansible_distribution_version }}.

  tasks:
    - name: Install system libraries needed to build R and Python packages
      ansible.builtin.apt:
        <<: *apt_defaults
        name:
          - build-essential
          - gfortran
          - libcurl4-openssl-dev
          - libssl-dev
          - libxml2-dev
          - libgit2-dev
          - libfontconfig1-dev
          - libharfbuzz-dev
          - libfribidi-dev
          - libudunits2-dev
          - libgdal-dev
          - pandoc
      tags: [system]

    - name: Add the CRAN apt repository
      ansible.builtin.deb822_repository:
        name: cran
        types: deb
        uris: https://cloud.r-project.org/bin/linux/ubuntu
        suites: "{{ ansible_distribution_release }}-cran40/"
        signed_by: https://cloud.r-project.org/bin/linux/ubuntu/marutter_pubkey.asc
        state: present
      tags: [r]

    - name: Install R {{ r_version }}
      ansible.builtin.apt:
        <<: *apt_defaults
        name: ["r-base={{ r_version }}-*", "r-base-dev={{ r_version }}-*"]
      tags: [r]

    - name: Write the site-wide Rprofile
      ansible.builtin.copy:
        dest: /etc/R/Rprofile.site
        owner: root
        group: root
        mode: "0644"
        content: |
          ## Managed by Ansible -- local changes will be overwritten.
          local({
            options(
              repos = c(CRAN = "{{ cran_repo }}"),
              HTTPUserAgent = sprintf(
                "R/%s R (%s)",
                getRversion(),
                paste(getRversion(), R.version["platform"], R.version["arch"], R.version["os"])
              ),
              Ncpus = {{ ansible_processor_vcpus | default(2) }}L
            )
          })
      tags: [r]

    - name: Install the lab's R packages
      ansible.builtin.command:
        cmd: >-
          Rscript -e 'pkgs <- c({{ r_packages | map("to_json") | join(", ") }});
          missing <- setdiff(pkgs, rownames(installed.packages()));
          if (length(missing)) install.packages(missing);
          cat(length(missing))'
      register: r_install
      changed_when: r_install.stdout | int > 0
      tags: [r, r_packages]

    - name: Install RStudio Server {{ rstudio_server_version }}
      ansible.builtin.apt:
        deb: "https://download2.rstudio.org/server/{{ ansible_distribution_release }}/amd64/rstudio-server-{{ rstudio_server_version }}-amd64.deb"
      notify: Restart rstudio-server
      tags: [rstudio]

    - name: Configure RStudio Server and R sessions
      ansible.builtin.copy:
        dest: "/etc/rstudio/{{ item.file }}"
        content: "{{ item.content }}"
        mode: "0644"
      loop:
        - file: rserver.conf
          content: |
            # Managed by Ansible
            www-port=8787
            auth-required-user-group={{ lab_group }}
        - file: rsession.conf
          content: |
            # Managed by Ansible
            session-timeout-minutes=480
            session-default-working-dir=~/projects
      loop_control:
        label: "{{ item.file }}"
      notify: Restart rstudio-server
      tags: [rstudio]

    - name: Install Miniforge into {{ miniforge_prefix }}
      ansible.builtin.shell:
        cmd: |
          set -euo pipefail
          curl -fsSL -o /tmp/miniforge.sh \
            "https://github.com/conda-forge/miniforge/releases/latest/download/Miniforge3-Linux-{{ ansible_architecture }}.sh"
          bash /tmp/miniforge.sh -b -p {{ miniforge_prefix }}
          rm -f /tmp/miniforge.sh
        creates: "{{ miniforge_prefix }}/bin/mamba"
        executable: /bin/bash
      tags: [python]

    - name: Copy the shared conda environment file
      ansible.builtin.template:
        src: templates/environment.yml.j2
        dest: "{{ miniforge_prefix }}/{{ conda_env_name }}.yml"
        mode: "0644"
      register: env_file
      tags: [python]

    - name: Create or update the shared conda environment
      ansible.builtin.command:
        cmd: "{{ miniforge_prefix }}/bin/mamba env update --name {{ conda_env_name }} --file {{ env_file.dest }} --prune"
      when: env_file is changed
      tags: [python]

    - name: Create the lab group
      ansible.builtin.group:
        name: "{{ lab_group }}"
        gid: 2100
      tags: [users]

    - name: Create lab user accounts
      ansible.builtin.user:
        name: "{{ item.name }}"
        uid: "{{ item.uid }}"
        shell: "{{ item.shell }}"
        groups: "{{ [lab_group] + (['sudo'] if item.admin else []) }}"
        append: true
      loop: "{{ lab_users }}"
      loop_control:
        label: "{{ item.name }}"
      tags: [users]

    - name: Allow SSH and RStudio Server from the campus network only
      community.general.ufw:
        rule: allow
        port: "{{ item }}"
        proto: tcp
        from_ip: 10.20.0.0/16
      loop: ["22", "8787"]
      tags: [firewall]

  post_tasks:
    - name: Summarise the installation
      ansible.builtin.debug:
        msg:
          - "R {{ r_version }} and RStudio Server {{ rstudio_server_version }} are ready on {{ inventory_hostname }}."
          - "RStudio Server: http://{{ ansible_host | default(inventory_hostname) }}:8787"
          - "Conda environment: {{ miniforge_prefix }}/envs/{{ conda_env_name }}"

  handlers:
    - name: Restart rstudio-server
      ansible.builtin.systemd:
        name: rstudio-server
        state: restarted

- name: Install CUDA on the GPU nodes for Stan and PyTorch
  hosts: gpu_nodes
  become: true
  tasks:
    - name: Install the NVIDIA driver and CUDA toolkit
      ansible.builtin.apt:
        <<: *apt_defaults
        name: [nvidia-driver-550, nvidia-cuda-toolkit]
      register: cuda_install

    - name: Reboot to load the new driver
      ansible.builtin.reboot:
        msg: "Rebooting {{ inventory_hostname }} to load the NVIDIA driver"
        reboot_timeout: 900
      when: cuda_install is changed

# survtrend (development version)

* `fit_trend()` now warns when a site has fewer than five survey years, because
  the site-level smoother is poorly identified in that case (#341).
* `read_survey()` gains an `encoding` argument. Files exported from the Windows version of the field app are now read correctly without manual re-encoding (@lmueller, #338).
* `autoplot()` uses the colour-blind-safe palette from the new `survtrend_palette()` helper by default (@nokafor, #344).

# survtrend 1.3.0

## Breaking changes

* `fit_model()` no longer silently drops sites with a single visit. These sites
  now trigger an error that lists the affected site IDs; set
  `drop_singletons = TRUE` to restore the previous behaviour (@amartin, #287).

* The `method` argument of `predict_trend()` has been renamed to `type` for
  consistency with `predict.glm()`. The old name still works but is deprecated
  and will be removed in survtrend 1.5.0 (#295).

## New features

* New `simulate_counts()` generates synthetic count data under a known trend, observer effect and detection probability, which is useful for power analyses and for checking custom model specifications before the field season starts (@nokafor, #301).

* `fit_model()` gains a `weights` argument that is passed on to the underlying engine for all supported families. Weights must be non-negative and are rescaled internally so that they sum to the number of observations (@jchen, #276).

* `autoplot.survtrend_fit()` gains a `type` argument. Use `type = "partial"` to
  draw partial-effect plots for individual smooth terms:

  ```r
  fit <- fit_model(count ~ s(year) + habitat, data = grassland_moths)
  autoplot(fit, type = "partial", terms = "s(year)")
  ```

* `tidy()` and `glance()` methods for `survtrend_fit` objects now return
  confidence intervals on the response scale when `exponentiate = TRUE`,
  matching the behaviour of the corresponding broom methods (#312).

## Minor improvements and fixes

* `check_design()` returns the number of visits per site and year as a tibble instead of printing a matrix, so the result can be filtered and joined with dplyr verbs (#305).
* Printing a `survtrend_fit` is much faster for models with many random-effect levels (@okafor-lab, #299).
* Error messages now use `cli::cli_abort()` throughout and link to the relevant help page, e.g. `` `effort` must be positive; see `?fit_trend` ``.
* The "Getting started" vignette now uses the bundled `grassland_moths` data and runs in under ten seconds, so it is no longer pre-computed.

## Bug fixes

* `fit_trend()` no longer fails when the `site` column is a factor with unused levels (@jchen, #318).
* `predict_trend()` returned standard errors on the link scale even when
  `type = "response"` was requested. They are now transformed with the delta
  method, and a new test compares them against a parametric bootstrap (#322).
* `read_survey()` correctly parses dates written as `dd.mm.yyyy`, which is the default in the German-language version of the field app (@lmueller, #327).
* Fixed a rare integer overflow in `simulate_counts()` when `n_sites * n_years * n_visits` exceeded `.Machine$integer.max` (#330).

# survtrend 1.2.1

This is a patch release to fix test failures on CRAN's r-devel machines caused by changes in R 4.5.0.

## Bug fixes

* Tests no longer depend on the exact wording of base R warning messages (#284).
* `fit_model()` now passes `control` arguments on to `glmmTMB::glmmTMB()` instead of silently ignoring them (@amartin, #281).

# survtrend 1.2.0

## New features

* Support for zero-inflated negative-binomial models via `family = "zinb"` in
  `fit_model()`. The zero-inflation probability can depend on covariates through
  the new `zi_formula` argument (#251).
* New `compare_trends()` computes pairwise differences between site-level trends, with p-values adjusted by any method supported by `p.adjust()` (@nokafor, #263).
* New vignette, "Choosing a model family", walks through overdispersion and zero-inflation diagnostics using simulated data and the `grassland_moths` dataset.

## Deprecations

* `trend_summary()` is deprecated in favour of `tidy()`. It now emits a
  deprecation warning once per session and will be removed in survtrend 1.4.0
  (#258).

## Bug fixes

* `autoplot()` no longer drops the confidence ribbon when the data contain only one site (#249).
* Missing effort values in `fit_trend()` are now dropped with a warning instead of producing `NaN` offsets that made the optimiser fail with an unhelpful message (@jchen, #255).

# survtrend 1.1.0

* survtrend now requires R >= 4.1.0 because it uses the native pipe `|>` and
  the `\(x)` lambda syntax internally.
* New `read_survey()` reads the CSV and Excel exports of the ecolab field app
  and validates them against the survey schema (#212, #219).
* `fit_trend()` gains several new arguments:
  * `effort`, the sampling effort, which enters the model as a `log(effort)` offset (@amartin, #224);
  * `min_years`, the minimum number of years a site must have been surveyed to
    be included (#226);
  * `k`, the basis dimension of the year smoother.
* Fixed a bug where `autoplot()` mislabelled the y axis for Poisson models (#230).

# survtrend 1.0.1

* Fixed a test that failed on 32-bit Windows because of floating-point tolerance (#205).
* Updated `CITATION` to point to the published version of the methods paper in *Methods in Ecology and Evolution*.

# survtrend 1.0.0

* First release on CRAN.
* Added a `NEWS.md` file to track changes to the package.

# Contributing to survtrend

Thank you for taking the time to contribute! survtrend is developed by the [Computational Ecology Lab](https://ecolab.example.edu) at the University of Example together with a small community of users from ecological monitoring programmes across Europe. This guide explains how to report problems, set up a development environment for the R and Python packages, and get a pull request merged.

This project is released with a [Contributor Code of Conduct](CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md). By participating in this project you agree to abide by its terms. Please report unacceptable behaviour to [conduct@ecolab.example.edu](mailto:conduct@ecolab.example.edu).

## Ways to contribute

- **Report a bug.** Open an [issue](https://github.com/ecolab-uni/survtrend/issues/new/choose) with a minimal reproducible example. For R code, the [reprex](https://reprex.tidyverse.org) package makes this much easier; for Python, paste the full traceback and the output of `survtrend.show_versions()`.
- **Improve the documentation.** Typos and small fixes can be made directly in the GitHub web interface. For anything larger, please open an issue first so that we can agree on the scope.
- **Propose a new feature.** Describe the use case *before* writing code. Features that only make sense for a single monitoring scheme may be better placed in a separate package.
- **Share a dataset.** We are always looking for real monitoring data, with permission to publish, that can be turned into vignettes or test cases.

## Repository layout

| Path | Contents |
|------|----------|
| `r/` | The R package, released on CRAN |
| `python/` | The Python package, published on PyPI and conda-forge |
| `docs/` | The shared Quarto website |
| `data-raw/` | Scripts that create the bundled example datasets |
| `tests/reference/` | Reference results shared by both test suites |

## Development setup

### R

You need R >= 4.1 and a toolchain for compiling packages: Rtools on Windows, the Xcode command line tools on macOS, and `r-base-dev` on Debian or Ubuntu.

```r
# install.packages(c("devtools", "pak"))
pak::local_install_dev_deps("r")
devtools::load_all("r")
```

`devtools::load_all()` simulates installing and attaching the package, so you can try out changes interactively without rebuilding it. When you are ready, run the tests and the full check:

```r
devtools::test("r")
devtools::check("r")
```

### Python

We use [mamba](https://mamba.readthedocs.io) or conda to manage the Python environment, because several dependencies (notably `netCDF4` and `cartopy`) are much easier to install from conda-forge than from PyPI.

```bash
mamba env create -f python/environment-dev.yml
mamba activate survtrend-dev
python -m pip install --no-deps -e "./python[dev]"
pre-commit install
```

The editable install means that changes under `python/src/survtrend/` are picked up without reinstalling. If you prefer not to use conda, `uv venv && uv pip install -e "./python[dev]"` works on Linux and macOS, but you will have to install GDAL and NetCDF yourself.

## Running the tests

- **R:** `devtools::test()` runs the testthat suite. Snapshot tests live in `r/tests/testthat/_snaps/`; review changed snapshots with `testthat::snapshot_review()` and commit them together with the code that changed them.
- **Python:** `pytest python/tests -n auto` runs the suite in parallel. Tests that fit full models are marked with `@pytest.mark.slow` and are skipped unless you pass `--runslow`.
- **Both:** the two implementations are tested against the same reference results in `tests/reference/`. If you change a numerical routine, regenerate them with `make reference` and explain in the pull request why the numbers changed.

## Making a pull request

1. Fork the repository on GitHub and clone your fork:

   ```bash
   git clone https://github.com/<your-username>/survtrend.git
   cd survtrend
   git remote add upstream https://github.com/ecolab-uni/survtrend.git
   ```

2. Create a branch from the latest `main` with a short, descriptive name:

   ```bash
   git fetch upstream
   git switch -c fix-offset-handling upstream/main
   ```

3. Make your changes and add tests. If you edited roxygen comments in the R package, regenerate the documentation:

   ```r
   devtools::document("r")
   ```

4. Add a bullet to the top of `NEWS.md` (and of `python/CHANGELOG.md` for Python changes) that describes the change, followed by your GitHub handle and the issue number, for example `(@yourname, #123)`.

5. Push the branch and open a pull request against `main`. A maintainer will review it once the continuous integration checks have passed. Please be patient: we are a small team, and teaching takes priority during term.

### Pull request checklist

Copy this list into the pull request description and tick the boxes that apply:

- [ ] The pull request is linked to an issue that describes the motivation.
- [ ] New code is covered by tests, and `devtools::check()` and `pytest` pass locally.
- [ ] User-facing changes are described in `NEWS.md` and, where relevant, in a vignette or the user guide.
- [ ] R code follows the [tidyverse style guide](https://style.tidyverse.org) (run `air format r/` or `styler::style_pkg("r")`); Python code passes `ruff check` and `ruff format --check`.
- [ ] Reference results were regenerated with `make reference` (only if numerical output changed).
- [ ] I have added myself to `DESCRIPTION` and `python/pyproject.toml` as a contributor (optional, but we would like to thank you!).

## Issue labels

We use the following labels to triage issues and pull requests:

| Label | Meaning |
|-------|---------|
| `bug` | Something does not work as documented |
| `feature` | A new capability, argument or function |
| `docs` | Documentation only |
| `good first issue` | A small, well-defined task suitable for new contributors |
| `help wanted` | We would welcome a pull request from the community |
| `r` / `python` | Affects only one of the two implementations |
| `upstream` | Caused by a dependency such as glmmTMB or xarray; tracked elsewhere |
| `needs reprex` | We cannot act on this until there is a reproducible example |

## Style and documentation

- Function and argument names use `snake_case` in both languages, and the R and Python APIs should match wherever the languages allow it.
- Document every exported R function with roxygen2, including at least one runnable example. Python docstrings follow the [NumPy docstring standard](https://numpydoc.readthedocs.io/en/latest/format.html).
- Write documentation in British English, consistent with the rest of the package ("behaviour", "modelling", "colour").
- Keep examples fast: CRAN expects each example to run in a few seconds, so use `\donttest{}` sparingly and only for genuinely slow model fits.

## Getting help

If you are stuck, open a draft pull request and ask; it is much easier to help when we can see the code. For general questions about modelling monitoring data, please use the [discussion forum](https://github.com/ecolab-uni/survtrend/discussions) rather than the issue tracker.

# Local development stack for survtrend.
#
# Copy `.env.example` to `.env`, then start the core services with
#
#   docker compose up -d
#   docker compose --profile docs up docs   # live preview of the website
#
# Services:
#   - RStudio Server    http://localhost:8787  (user "rstudio", password from .env)
#   - JupyterLab        http://localhost:8888
#   - Survey Data API   http://localhost:8000/docs
#   - MinIO console     http://localhost:9001

name: survtrend-dev

x-db-env: &db-env
  PGHOST: db
  PGPORT: "5432"
  PGDATABASE: ${POSTGRES_DB:-surveys}
  PGUSER: ${POSTGRES_USER:-ecolab}
  PGPASSWORD: ${POSTGRES_PASSWORD:?Set POSTGRES_PASSWORD in .env}
  TZ: Europe/Berlin

x-healthcheck: &default-healthcheck
  interval: 30s
  timeout: 10s
  retries: 5
  start_period: 20s

x-logging: &default-logging
  driver: json-file
  options:
    max-size: "10m"
    max-file: "3"

services:
  db:
    image: postgis/postgis:16-3.4
    restart: unless-stopped
    environment:
      POSTGRES_DB: ${POSTGRES_DB:-surveys}
      POSTGRES_USER: ${POSTGRES_USER:-ecolab}
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: ${POSTGRES_PASSWORD:?Set POSTGRES_PASSWORD in .env}
      TZ: Europe/Berlin
    volumes:
      - pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data
      # Scripts in this folder run once, when the data volume is empty.
      - ./db/init:/docker-entrypoint-initdb.d:ro
    ports:
      - "127.0.0.1:5432:5432"
    healthcheck:
      <<: *default-healthcheck
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "pg_isready -U $${POSTGRES_USER} -d $${POSTGRES_DB}"]
    logging: *default-logging

  rstudio:
    image: rocker/geospatial:4.4.2
    restart: unless-stopped
    depends_on:

        condition: service_healthy
    environment:

# Provision the shared analysis servers of the Computational Ecology Lab.
#
# Installs R from the CRAN apt repository, RStudio Server and a Miniforge-based
# Python stack, then creates the lab user accounts.
#
# Usage:
#   ansible-playbook -i inventories/lab.ini ansible_playbook.yml --ask-become-pass
#   ansible-playbook -i inventories/lab.ini ansible_playbook.yml --tags r_packages
#
# Maintainer: Lena Müller <l.mueller@ecolab.example.edu>

- name: Provision shared analysis servers
  hosts: analysis_servers
  become: true
  gather_facts: true

  vars:
    r_version: "4.4.2"
    rstudio_server_version: "2024.12.0-467"
    miniforge_prefix: /opt/miniforge3
    conda_env_name: ecolab-py312
    lab_group: ecolab
    lab_users:
      - { name: amartin, uid: 2101, shell: /bin/bash, admin: true }
      - { name: jchen, uid: 2102, shell: /bin/zsh, admin: false }
      - { name: nokafor, uid: 2103, shell: /bin/bash, admin: false }
      - { name: lmueller, uid: 2104, shell: /bin/bash, admin: true }
    # Binary packages for Ubuntu from Posit Public Package Manager; much faster
    # than compiling the geospatial stack from source after every R upgrade.
    cran_repo: "https://packagemanager.posit.co/cran/__linux__/{{ ansible_distribution_release }}/latest"
    r_packages: [tidyverse, lme4, glmmTMB, brms, targets, renv, devtools, rmarkdown, sf, terra, unmarked]
    apt_defaults: &apt_defaults
      update_cache: true
      cache_valid_time: 3600
      state: present

  pre_tasks:
    - name: Fail early on unsupported distributions
      ansible.builtin.assert:
        that:
          - ansible_distribution == "Ubuntu"
          - ansible_distribution_version is version("22.04", ">=")
        fail_msg: >-
          This playbook only supports Ubuntu 22.04 or newer, but
          {{ inventory_hostname }} runs {{ ansible_distribution }}
          {{ ansible_distribution_version }}.

  tasks:
    - name: Install system libraries needed to build R and Python packages
      ansible.builtin.apt:
        <<: *apt_defaults
        name:
          - build-essential
          - gfortran
          - libcurl4-openssl-dev
          - libssl-dev
          - libxml2-dev
          - libgit2-dev
          - libfontconfig1-dev
          - libharfbuzz-dev
          - libfribidi-dev
          - libudunits2-dev
          - libgdal-dev
          - pandoc
      tags: [system]

    - name: Add the CRAN apt repository
      ansible.builtin.deb822_repository:
        name: cran
        types: deb
        uris: https://cloud.r-project.org/bin/linux/ubuntu
        suites: "{{ ansible_distribution_release }}-cran40/"
        signed_by: https://cloud.r-project.org/bin/linux/ubuntu/marutter_pubkey.asc
        state: present
      tags: [r]

    - name: Install R {{ r_version }}
      ansible.builtin.apt:
        <<: *apt_defaults
        name: ["r-base={{ r_version }}-*", "r-base-dev={{ r_version }}-*"]
      tags: [r]

    - name: Write the site-wide Rprofile
      ansible.builtin.copy:
        dest: /etc/R/Rprofile.site
        owner: root
        group: root
        mode: "0644"
        content: |
          ## Managed by Ansible -- local changes will be overwritten.
          local({
            options(
              repos = c(CRAN = "{{ cran_repo }}"),
              HTTPUserAgent = sprintf(
                "R/%s R (%s)",
                getRversion(),
                paste(getRversion(), R.version["platform"], R.version["arch"], R.version["os"])
              ),
              Ncpus = {{ ansible_processor_vcpus | default(2) }}L
            )
          })
      tags: [r]

    - name: Install the lab's R packages
      ansible.builtin.command:
        cmd: >-
          Rscript -e 'pkgs <- c({{ r_packages | map("to_json") | join(", ") }});
          missing <- setdiff(pkgs, rownames(installed.packages()));
          if (length(missing)) install.packages(missing);
          cat(length(missing))'
      register: r_install
      changed_when: r_install.stdout | int > 0
      tags: [r, r_packages]

    - name: Install RStudio Server {{ rstudio_server_version }}
      ansible.builtin.apt:
        deb: "https://download2.rstudio.org/server/{{ ansible_distribution_release }}/amd64/rstudio-server-{{ rstudio_server_version }}-amd64.deb"
      notify: Restart rstudio-server
      tags: [rstudio]

    - name: Configure RStudio Server and R sessions
      ansible.builtin.copy:
        dest: "/etc/rstudio/{{ item.file }}"
        content: "{{ item.content }}"
        mode: "0644"
      loop:
        - file: rserver.conf
          content: |
            # Managed by Ansible
            www-port=8787
            auth-required-user-group={{ lab_group }}
        - file: rsession.conf
          content: |
            # Managed by Ansible
            session-timeout-minutes=480
            session-default-working-dir=~/projects
      loop_control:
        label: "{{ item.file }}"
      notify: Restart rstudio-server
      tags: [rstudio]

    - name: Install Miniforge into {{ miniforge_prefix }}
      ansible.builtin.shell:
        cmd: |
          set -euo pipefail
          curl -fsSL -o /tmp/miniforge.sh \
            "https://github.com/conda-forge/miniforge/releases/latest/download/Miniforge3-Linux-{{ ansible_architecture }}.sh"
          bash /tmp/miniforge.sh -b -p {{ miniforge_prefix }}
          rm -f /tmp/miniforge.sh
        creates: "{{ miniforge_prefix }}/bin/mamba"
        executable: /bin/bash
      tags: [python]

    - name: Copy the shared conda environment file
      ansible.builtin.template:
        src: templates/environment.yml.j2
        dest: "{{ miniforge_prefix }}/{{ conda_env_name }}.yml"
        mode: "0644"
      register: env_file
      tags: [python]

    - name: Create or update the shared conda environment
      ansible.builtin.command:
        cmd: "{{ miniforge_prefix }}/bin/mamba env update --name {{ conda_env_name }} --file {{ env_file.dest }} --prune"
      when: env_file is changed
      tags: [python]

    - name: Create the lab group
      ansible.builtin.group:
        name: "{{ lab_group }}"
        gid: 2100
      tags: [users]

    - name: Create lab user accounts
      ansible.builtin.user:
        name: "{{ item.name }}"
        uid: "{{ item.uid }}"
        shell: "{{ item.shell }}"
        groups: "{{ [lab_group] + (['sudo'] if item.admin else []) }}"
        append: true
      loop: "{{ lab_users }}"
      loop_control:
        label: "{{ item.name }}"
      tags: [users]

    - name: Allow SSH and RStudio Server from the campus network only
      community.general.ufw:
        rule: allow
        port: "{{ item }}"
        proto: tcp
        from_ip: 10.20.0.0/16
      loop: ["22", "8787"]
      tags: [firewall]

  post_tasks:
    - name: Summarise the installation
      ansible.builtin.debug:
        msg:
          - "R {{ r_version }} and RStudio Server {{ rstudio_server_version }} are ready on {{ inventory_hostname }}."
          - "RStudio Server: http://{{ ansible_host | default(inventory_hostname) }}:8787"
          - "Conda environment: {{ miniforge_prefix }}/envs/{{ conda_env_name }}"

  handlers:
    - name: Restart rstudio-server
      ansible.builtin.systemd:
        name: rstudio-server
        state: restarted

- name: Install CUDA on the GPU nodes for Stan and PyTorch
  hosts: gpu_nodes
  become: true
  tasks:
    - name: Install the NVIDIA driver and CUDA toolkit
      ansible.builtin.apt:
        <<: *apt_defaults
        name: [nvidia-driver-550, nvidia-cuda-toolkit]
      register: cuda_install

    - name: Reboot to load the new driver
      ansible.builtin.reboot:
        msg: "Rebooting {{ inventory_hostname }} to load the NVIDIA driver"
        reboot_timeout: 900
      when: cuda_install is changed

# survtrend (development version)

* `fit_trend()` now warns when a site has fewer than five survey years, because
  the site-level smoother is poorly identified in that case (#341).
* `read_survey()` gains an `encoding` argument. Files exported from the Windows version of the field app are now read correctly without manual re-encoding (@lmueller, #338).
* `autoplot()` uses the colour-blind-safe palette from the new `survtrend_palette()` helper by default (@nokafor, #344).

# survtrend 1.3.0

## Breaking changes

* `fit_model()` no longer silently drops sites with a single visit. These sites
  now trigger an error that lists the affected site IDs; set
  `drop_singletons = TRUE` to restore the previous behaviour (@amartin, #287).

* The `method` argument of `predict_trend()` has been renamed to `type` for
  consistency with `predict.glm()`. The old name still works but is deprecated
  and will be removed in survtrend 1.5.0 (#295).

## New features

* New `simulate_counts()` generates synthetic count data under a known trend, observer effect and detection probability, which is useful for power analyses and for checking custom model specifications before the field season starts (@nokafor, #301).

* `fit_model()` gains a `weights` argument that is passed on to the underlying engine for all supported families. Weights must be non-negative and are rescaled internally so that they sum to the number of observations (@jchen, #276).

* `autoplot.survtrend_fit()` gains a `type` argument. Use `type = "partial"` to
  draw partial-effect plots for individual smooth terms:

  ```r
  fit <- fit_model(count ~ s(year) + habitat, data = grassland_moths)
  autoplot(fit, type = "partial", terms = "s(year)")
  ```

* `tidy()` and `glance()` methods for `survtrend_fit` objects now return
  confidence intervals on the response scale when `exponentiate = TRUE`,
  matching the behaviour of the corresponding broom methods (#312).

## Minor improvements and fixes

* `check_design()` returns the number of visits per site and year as a tibble instead of printing a matrix, so the result can be filtered and joined with dplyr verbs (#305).
* Printing a `survtrend_fit` is much faster for models with many random-effect levels (@okafor-lab, #299).
* Error messages now use `cli::cli_abort()` throughout and link to the relevant help page, e.g. `` `effort` must be positive; see `?fit_trend` ``.
* The "Getting started" vignette now uses the bundled `grassland_moths` data and runs in under ten seconds, so it is no longer pre-computed.

## Bug fixes

* `fit_trend()` no longer fails when the `site` column is a factor with unused levels (@jchen, #318).
* `predict_trend()` returned standard errors on the link scale even when
  `type = "response"` was requested. They are now transformed with the delta
  method, and a new test compares them against a parametric bootstrap (#322).
* `read_survey()` correctly parses dates written as `dd.mm.yyyy`, which is the default in the German-language version of the field app (@lmueller, #327).
* Fixed a rare integer overflow in `simulate_counts()` when `n_sites * n_years * n_visits` exceeded `.Machine$integer.max` (#330).

# survtrend 1.2.1

This is a patch release to fix test failures on CRAN's r-devel machines caused by changes in R 4.5.0.

## Bug fixes

* Tests no longer depend on the exact wording of base R warning messages (#284).
* `fit_model()` now passes `control` arguments on to `glmmTMB::glmmTMB()` instead of silently ignoring them (@amartin, #281).

# survtrend 1.2.0

## New features

* Support for zero-inflated negative-binomial models via `family = "zinb"` in
  `fit_model()`. The zero-inflation probability can depend on covariates through
  the new `zi_formula` argument (#251).
* New `compare_trends()` computes pairwise differences between site-level trends, with p-values adjusted by any method supported by `p.adjust()` (@nokafor, #263).
* New vignette, "Choosing a model family", walks through overdispersion and zero-inflation diagnostics using simulated data and the `grassland_moths` dataset.

## Deprecations

* `trend_summary()` is deprecated in favour of `tidy()`. It now emits a
  deprecation warning once per session and will be removed in survtrend 1.4.0
  (#258).

## Bug fixes

* `autoplot()` no longer drops the confidence ribbon when the data contain only one site (#249).
* Missing effort values in `fit_trend()` are now dropped with a warning instead of producing `NaN` offsets that made the optimiser fail with an unhelpful message (@jchen, #255).

# survtrend 1.1.0

* survtrend now requires R >= 4.1.0 because it uses the native pipe `|>` and
  the `\(x)` lambda syntax internally.
* New `read_survey()` reads the CSV and Excel exports of the ecolab field app
  and validates them against the survey schema (#212, #219).
* `fit_trend()` gains several new arguments:
  * `effort`, the sampling effort, which enters the model as a `log(effort)` offset (@amartin, #224);
  * `min_years`, the minimum number of years a site must have been surveyed to
    be included (#226);
  * `k`, the basis dimension of the year smoother.

* Fixed a test that failed on 32-bit Windows because of floating-point tolerance (#205).

# Contributing to survtrend

Thank you for taking the time to contribute! survtrend is developed by the [Computational Ecology Lab](https://ecolab.example.edu) at the University of Example together with a small community of users from ecological monitoring programmes across Europe. This guide explains how to report problems, set up a development environment for the R and Python packages, and get a pull request merged.

This project is released with a [Contributor Code of Conduct](CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md). By participating in this project you agree to abide by its terms. Please report unacceptable behaviour to [conduct@ecolab.example.edu](mailto:conduct@ecolab.example.edu).

## Ways to contribute

- **Report a bug.** Open an [issue](https://github.com/ecolab-uni/survtrend/issues/new/choose) with a minimal reproducible example. For R code, the [reprex](https://reprex.tidyverse.org) package makes this much easier; for Python, paste the full traceback and the output of `survtrend.show_versions()`.
- **Improve the documentation.** Typos and small fixes can be made directly in the GitHub web interface. For anything larger, please open an issue first so that we can agree on the scope.
- **Propose a new feature.** Describe the use case *before* writing code. Features that only make sense for a single monitoring scheme may be better placed in a separate package.
- **Share a dataset.** We are always looking for real monitoring data, with permission to publish, that can be turned into vignettes or test cases.

## Repository layout

| Path | Contents |
|------|----------|
| `r/` | The R package, released on CRAN |
| `python/` | The Python package, published on PyPI and conda-forge |
| `docs/` | The shared Quarto website |
| `data-raw/` | Scripts that create the bundled example datasets |
| `tests/reference/` | Reference results shared by both test suites |

## Development setup

### R

You need R >= 4.1 and a toolchain for compiling packages: Rtools on Windows, the Xcode command line tools on macOS, and `r-base-dev` on Debian or Ubuntu.

```r
# install.packages(c("devtools", "pak"))
pak::local_install_dev_deps("r")
devtools::load_all("r")
```

`devtools::load_all()` simulates installing and attaching the package, so you can try out changes interactively without rebuilding it. When you are ready, run the tests and the full check:

```r
devtools::test("r")
devtools::check("r")
```

### Python

We use [mamba](https://mamba.readthedocs.io) or conda to manage the Python environment, because several dependencies (notably `netCDF4` and `cartopy`) are much easier to install from conda-forge than from PyPI.

```bash
mamba env create -f python/environment-dev.yml
mamba activate survtrend-dev
python -m pip install --no-deps -e "./python[dev]"
pre-commit install
```

The editable install means that changes under `python/src/survtrend/` are picked up without reinstalling. If you prefer not to use conda, `uv venv && uv pip install -e "./python[dev]"` works on Linux and macOS, but you will have to install GDAL and NetCDF yourself.

## Running the tests

- **R:** `devtools::test()` runs the testthat suite. Snapshot tests live in `r/tests/testthat/_snaps/`; review changed snapshots with `testthat::snapshot_review()` and commit them together with the code that changed them.
- **Python:** `pytest python/tests -n auto` runs the suite in parallel. Tests that fit full models are marked with `@pytest.mark.slow` and are skipped unless you pass `--runslow`.
- **Both:** the two implementations are tested against the same reference results in `tests/reference/`. If you change a numerical routine, regenerate them with `make reference` and explain in the pull request why the numbers changed.

## Making a pull request

1. Fork the repository on GitHub and clone your fork:

   ```bash
   git clone https://github.com/<your-username>/survtrend.git
   cd survtrend
   git remote add upstream https://github.com/ecolab-uni/survtrend.git
   ```

2. Create a branch from the latest `main` with a short, descriptive name:

   ```bash
   git fetch upstream
   git switch -c fix-offset-handling upstream/main
   ```

3. Make your changes and add tests. If you edited roxygen comments in the R package, regenerate the documentation:

   ```r
   devtools::document("r")
   ```

4. Add a bullet to the top of `NEWS.md` (and of `python/CHANGELOG.md` for Python changes) that describes the change, followed by your GitHub handle and the issue number, for example `(@yourname, #123)`.

5. Push the branch and open a pull request against `main`. A maintainer will review it once the continuous integration checks have passed. Please be patient: we are a small team, and teaching takes priority during term.

### Pull request checklist

Copy this list into the pull request description and tick the boxes that apply:

- [ ] The pull request is linked to an issue that describes the motivation.
- [ ] New code is covered by tests, and `devtools::check()` and `pytest` pass locally.
- [ ] User-facing changes are described in `NEWS.md` and, where relevant, in a vignette or the user guide.
- [ ] R code follows the [tidyverse style guide](https://style.tidyverse.org) (run `air format r/` or `styler::style_pkg("r")`); Python code passes `ruff check` and `ruff format --check`.
- [ ] Reference results were regenerated with `make reference` (only if numerical output changed).
- [ ] I have added myself to `DESCRIPTION` and `python/pyproject.toml` as a contributor (optional, but we would like to thank you!).

## Issue labels

We use the following labels to triage issues and pull requests:

| Label | Meaning |
|-------|---------|
| `bug` | Something does not work as documented |
| `feature` | A new capability, argument or function |
| `docs` | Documentation only |
| `good first issue` | A small, well-defined task suitable for new contributors |
| `help wanted` | We would welcome a pull request from the community |
| `r` / `python` | Affects only one of the two implementations |
| `upstream` | Caused by a dependency such as glmmTMB or xarray; tracked elsewhere |
| `needs reprex` | We cannot act on this until there is a reproducible example |

## Style and documentation

- Function and argument names use `snake_case` in both languages, and the R and Python APIs should match wherever the languages allow it.
- Document every exported R function with roxygen2, including at least one runnable example. Python docstrings follow the [NumPy docstring standard](https://numpydoc.readthedocs.io/en/latest/format.html).
- Write documentation in British English, consistent with the rest of the package ("behaviour", "modelling", "colour").
- Keep examples fast: CRAN expects each example to run in a few seconds, so use `\donttest{}` sparingly and only for genuinely slow model fits.

## Getting help

If you are stuck, open a draft pull request and ask; it is much easier to help when we can see the code. For general questions about modelling monitoring data, please use the [discussion forum](https://github.com/ecolab-uni/survtrend/discussions) rather than the issue tracker.

    environment:

# Workflow derived from https://github.com/r-lib/actions/tree/v2/examples
# Need help debugging build failures? Start at https://github.com/r-lib/actions#where-to-find-help
#
# Runs R CMD check on the R package and pytest on the Python package. The
# weekly scheduled run catches breakage caused by new releases of upstream
# dependencies (glmmTMB, mgcv, xarray, ...) before our users run into it.
on:
  push:
    branches: [main, "release/**"]
    paths-ignore:
      - "docs/**"
      - "**.md"
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]
  schedule:
    # Mondays at 05:17 UTC, away from the busy top of the hour
    - cron: "17 5 * * 1"
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      run-slow-tests:
        description: "Also run the slow Python tests that fit full models"
        type: boolean
        default: false

name: R-CMD-check

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.event.pull_request.number || github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  R-CMD-check:
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.config.os }}

    name: R ${{ matrix.config.r }} (${{ matrix.config.os }})

    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        config:
          - {os: macos-latest,   r: 'release'}
          - {os: windows-latest, r: 'release'}
          - {os: ubuntu-latest,  r: 'devel', http-user-agent: 'release'}
          - {os: ubuntu-latest,  r: 'release'}
          - {os: ubuntu-latest,  r: 'oldrel-1'}
          # Minimum supported version, see Depends in r/DESCRIPTION
          - {os: ubuntu-latest,  r: '4.1'}

    env:
      GITHUB_PAT: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
      R_KEEP_PKG_SOURCE: yes
      _R_CHECK_CRAN_INCOMING_: false

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: r-lib/actions/setup-pandoc@v2

      - uses: r-lib/actions/setup-r@v2
        with:
          r-version: ${{ matrix.config.r }}
          http-user-agent: ${{ matrix.config.http-user-agent }}
          use-public-rspm: true

      - uses: r-lib/actions/setup-r-dependencies@v2
        with:
          working-directory: r
          extra-packages: any::rcmdcheck
          needs: check
          # Bump to invalidate the package cache after a broken upstream release
          cache-version: 3

      - uses: r-lib/actions/check-r-package@v2
        with:
          working-directory: r
          upload-snapshots: true
          build_args: 'c("--no-manual", "--compact-vignettes=gs+qpdf")'
          error-on: '"warning"'

  pytest:
    name: Python ${{ matrix.python-version }} (${{ matrix.os }})
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}

    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        os: [ubuntu-latest, macos-latest, windows-latest]
        python-version: ["3.10", "3.11", "3.12", "3.13"]
        exclude:
          - os: macos-latest
            python-version: "3.10"
          - os: windows-latest
            python-version: "3.10"
        include:
          - os: ubuntu-latest
            python-version: "3.12"
            coverage: true

    defaults:
      run:
        shell: bash -el {0}
        working-directory: python

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Set up the micromamba environment
        uses: mamba-org/setup-micromamba@v2
        with:
          environment-file: python/environment-dev.yml
          environment-name: survtrend-dev
          create-args: >-
            python=${{ matrix.python-version }}
          cache-environment: true
          cache-environment-key: env-${{ runner.os }}-py${{ matrix.python-version }}-${{ hashFiles('python/environment-dev.yml') }}

      - name: Cache downloaded test data
        uses: actions/cache@v4
        with:
          path: |
            ~/.cache/survtrend
            python/.hypothesis
          key: testdata-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('tests/reference/**') }}
          restore-keys: |
            testdata-${{ runner.os }}-

      - name: Install survtrend
        run: python -m pip install --no-deps -e ".[dev]"

      - name: Run pytest
        env:
          RUN_SLOW: ${{ github.event_name == 'schedule' || inputs.run-slow-tests }}
          COV_ARGS: ${{ matrix.coverage && '--cov=survtrend --cov-report=xml' || '' }}
        run: |
          extra_args=()
          if [[ "$RUN_SLOW" == "true" ]]; then
            extra_args+=(--runslow)
          fi
          pytest tests -n auto --durations=20 $COV_ARGS "${extra_args[@]}"

      - name: Upload coverage to Codecov
        if: matrix.coverage && github.repository == 'ecolab-uni/survtrend'
        uses: codecov/codecov-action@v5
        with:
          files: python/coverage.xml
          flags: python
          token: ${{ secrets.CODECOV_TOKEN }}
          fail_ci_if_error: false

  reference-results:
    # Both implementations must reproduce the shared reference results.
    needs: [R-CMD-check, pytest]
    if: github.event_name != 'schedule'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: r-lib/actions/setup-r@v2
        with:
          use-public-rspm: true

      - uses: r-lib/actions/setup-r-dependencies@v2
        with:
          working-directory: r
          extra-packages: local::.

      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: "3.12"
          cache: pip
          cache-dependency-path: python/pyproject.toml

      - name: Compare R and Python results
        run: |
          python -m pip install ./python
          make -C tests/reference compare TOLERANCE=1e-6

# Kubernetes manifests for the survtrend Shiny dashboard and the lab's
# JupyterHub user profiles. Apply with:
#
#   kubectl apply -f kubernetes_multi_document.yaml
#
# The cluster runs ingress-nginx and cert-manager. JupyterHub itself is
# installed with the zero-to-jupyterhub Helm chart (infra/jupyterhub/values.yaml).
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: shiny-server-config
  namespace: ecolab-apps
data:
  shiny-server.conf: |
    # Run applications as the unprivileged "shiny" user
    run_as shiny;
    preserve_logs true;
    sanitize_errors true;

    server {
      listen 3838;

      location / {
        site_dir /srv/shiny-server/survtrend-dashboard;
        log_dir /var/log/shiny-server;
        directory_index off;
        app_idle_timeout 600;
        app_init_timeout 120;
      }
    }
  DASHBOARD_TITLE: "Grassland insect monitoring – survtrend dashboard"
  API_BASE_URL: "http://survey-api.ecolab-apps.svc.cluster.local:8000/v1"
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: dashboard-db-credentials
  namespace: ecolab-apps
type: Opaque
stringData:
  PGHOST: postgres.ecolab-data.svc.cluster.local
  PGDATABASE: surveys
  PGUSER: dashboard_ro
  # Placeholder only: the real value is managed by sealed-secrets.
  PGPASSWORD: "REPLACE_ME"
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
metadata:
  name: dashboard-cache
  namespace: ecolab-apps
spec:
  accessModes: [ReadWriteMany]
  storageClassName: nfs-client
  resources:
    requests:
      storage: 5Gi
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: survtrend-dashboard
  namespace: ecolab-apps
  labels: &dashboard-labels
    app.kubernetes.io/name: survtrend-dashboard
    app.kubernetes.io/component: shiny
    app.kubernetes.io/part-of: survtrend
  annotations:
    kubernetes.io/change-cause: "Update to survtrend 1.3.0 for the autumn 2026 monitoring report"
spec:
  replicas: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels: *dashboard-labels
  strategy:
    type: RollingUpdate
    rollingUpdate: {maxSurge: 1, maxUnavailable: 0}
  template:
    metadata:
      labels: *dashboard-labels
    spec:
      securityContext:
        runAsUser: 999
        runAsGroup: 999
        fsGroup: 999
      containers:
        - name: shiny
          image: ghcr.io/ecolab-uni/survtrend-dashboard:1.3.0
          imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent
          ports:
            - name: http
              containerPort: 3838
          envFrom:
            - secretRef:
                name: dashboard-db-credentials
          env:
            - name: DASHBOARD_TITLE
              valueFrom:
                configMapKeyRef: {name: shiny-server-config, key: DASHBOARD_TITLE}
            - name: API_BASE_URL
              valueFrom:
                configMapKeyRef: {name: shiny-server-config, key: API_BASE_URL}
            - name: R_CONFIG_ACTIVE
              value: production
          resources:
            requests: {cpu: 250m, memory: 512Mi}
            limits: {cpu: "1", memory: 2Gi}
          readinessProbe:
            httpGet: {path: /, port: http}
            initialDelaySeconds: 15
            periodSeconds: 10
          livenessProbe:
            httpGet: {path: /, port: http}
            initialDelaySeconds: 60
            periodSeconds: 30
            failureThreshold: 3
          volumeMounts:
            - name: config
              mountPath: /etc/shiny-server/shiny-server.conf
              subPath: shiny-server.conf
            - name: cache
              mountPath: /srv/cache
      volumes:
        - name: config
          configMap:
            name: shiny-server-config
        - name: cache
          persistentVolumeClaim:
            claimName: dashboard-cache
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: survtrend-dashboard
  namespace: ecolab-apps
spec:
  selector:
    app.kubernetes.io/name: survtrend-dashboard
    app.kubernetes.io/component: shiny
  ports:
    - name: http
      port: 80
      targetPort: http
---
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: Ingress
metadata:
  name: survtrend-dashboard
  namespace: ecolab-apps
  annotations:
    cert-manager.io/cluster-issuer: letsencrypt-prod
    # Shiny keeps per-session state in the R process, so all requests of a
    # session must reach the same pod (sticky sessions via a cookie).
    nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/affinity: cookie
    nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/session-cookie-name: shiny-route
    nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/session-cookie-max-age: "28800"
    nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/proxy-read-timeout: "3600"
    nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/proxy-send-timeout: "3600"
spec:
  ingressClassName: nginx
  tls:
    - hosts: [dashboard.ecolab.example.edu]
      secretName: dashboard-tls
  rules:
    - host: dashboard.ecolab.example.edu
      http:
        paths:
          - path: /
            pathType: Prefix
            backend:
              service:
                name: survtrend-dashboard
                port:
                  name: http
---
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: CronJob
metadata:
  name: refresh-trend-cache
  namespace: ecolab-apps
spec:
  # Refit the site-level trends every night so that the dashboard opens quickly.
  schedule: "30 2 * * *"
  timeZone: Europe/Berlin
  concurrencyPolicy: Forbid
  jobTemplate:
    spec:
      backoffLimit: 2
      template:
        spec:
          restartPolicy: OnFailure
          containers:
            - name: refresh
              image: ghcr.io/ecolab-uni/survtrend-dashboard:1.3.0
              command: ["Rscript", "-e"]
              args:
                - |
                  library(survtrend)
                  con <- DBI::dbConnect(RPostgres::Postgres())
                  surveys <- read_survey(con, table = "catches_harmonised")
                  fits <- fit_trend(surveys, by = "site_id", family = "tweedie")
                  saveRDS(fits, "/srv/cache/trend-fits.rds")
                  DBI::dbDisconnect(con)
              envFrom:
                - secretRef: {name: dashboard-db-credentials}
              volumeMounts:
                - {name: cache, mountPath: /srv/cache}
          volumes:
            - name: cache
              persistentVolumeClaim: {claimName: dashboard-cache}
---
# Extra single-user profiles for JupyterHub, mounted into the hub pod and
# loaded from hub.extraConfig in the Helm values.
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: jupyterhub-profiles
  namespace: ecolab-jupyter
data:
  profiles.yaml: |
    - display_name: "Python 3.12 (survtrend, 4 CPU / 16 GB)"
      slug: survtrend-py
      default: true
      kubespawner_override:
        image: ghcr.io/ecolab-uni/survtrend-notebook:2026.11
        cpu_limit: 4
        mem_limit: 16G
    - display_name: "R 4.4 with RStudio (2 CPU / 8 GB)"
      slug: rstudio
      kubespawner_override:
        image: rocker/binder:4.4.2
        default_url: /rstudio
        cpu_limit: 2
        mem_limit: 8G

  icon:
    repo: fontawesome/brands/github
  palette:
    - media: "(prefers-color-scheme: light)"
      scheme: default
      primary: teal
      accent: amber
      toggle:
        icon: material/weather-night
        name: Switch to dark mode
    - media: "(prefers-color-scheme: dark)"
      scheme: slate
      primary: teal
      accent: amber
      toggle:
        icon: material/weather-sunny
        name: Switch to light mode

    - content.code.annotate
    - content.code.copy
    - content.tabs.link
    - navigation.footer
    - navigation.indexes
    - navigation.sections
    - navigation.tabs
    - navigation.top
    - search.highlight
    - search.suggest
    - toc.follow

watch:
  - src/survtrend

  - search
  - autorefs
  - gen-files:

            - https://docs.python.org/3/objects.inv
            - https://numpy.org/doc/stable/objects.inv
            - https://pandas.pydata.org/docs/objects.inv
            - https://docs.xarray.dev/en/stable/objects.inv
            - https://docs.scipy.org/doc/scipy/objects.inv

  - pymdownx.superfences:

#
# Runs R CMD check on the R package and pytest on the Python package. The
# weekly scheduled run catches breakage caused by new releases of upstream
# dependencies (glmmTMB, mgcv, xarray, ...) before our users run into it.
on:
  push:
    branches: [main, "release/**"]
    paths-ignore:
      - "docs/**"
      - "**.md"
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]
  schedule:
    # Mondays at 05:17 UTC, away from the busy top of the hour
    - cron: "17 5 * * 1"
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      run-slow-tests:
        description: "Also run the slow Python tests that fit full models"
        type: boolean
        default: false

name: R-CMD-check

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.event.pull_request.number || github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  R-CMD-check:
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.config.os }}

    name: R ${{ matrix.config.r }} (${{ matrix.config.os }})

    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        config:
          - {os: macos-latest,   r: 'release'}
          - {os: windows-latest, r: 'release'}
          - {os: ubuntu-latest,  r: 'devel', http-user-agent: 'release'}
          - {os: ubuntu-latest,  r: 'release'}
          - {os: ubuntu-latest,  r: 'oldrel-1'}
          # Minimum supported version, see Depends in r/DESCRIPTION
          - {os: ubuntu-latest,  r: '4.1'}

    env:
      GITHUB_PAT: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
      R_KEEP_PKG_SOURCE: yes
      _R_CHECK_CRAN_INCOMING_: false

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: r-lib/actions/setup-pandoc@v2

      - uses: r-lib/actions/setup-r@v2
        with:
          r-version: ${{ matrix.config.r }}
          http-user-agent: ${{ matrix.config.http-user-agent }}
          use-public-rspm: true

      - uses: r-lib/actions/setup-r-dependencies@v2
        with:
          working-directory: r
          extra-packages: any::rcmdcheck
          needs: check
          # Bump to invalidate the package cache after a broken upstream release
          cache-version: 3

      - uses: r-lib/actions/check-r-package@v2
        with:
          working-directory: r
          upload-snapshots: true
          build_args: 'c("--no-manual", "--compact-vignettes=gs+qpdf")'
          error-on: '"warning"'

  pytest:
    name: Python ${{ matrix.python-version }} (${{ matrix.os }})
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}

    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        os: [ubuntu-latest, macos-latest, windows-latest]
        python-version: ["3.10", "3.11", "3.12", "3.13"]
        exclude:
          - os: macos-latest
            python-version: "3.10"
          - os: windows-latest
            python-version: "3.10"
        include:
          - os: ubuntu-latest
            python-version: "3.12"
            coverage: true

    defaults:
      run:
        shell: bash -el {0}
        working-directory: python

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Set up the micromamba environment
        uses: mamba-org/setup-micromamba@v2
        with:
          environment-file: python/environment-dev.yml
          environment-name: survtrend-dev
          create-args: >-
            python=${{ matrix.python-version }}
          cache-environment: true
          cache-environment-key: env-${{ runner.os }}-py${{ matrix.python-version }}-${{ hashFiles('python/environment-dev.yml') }}

      - name: Cache downloaded test data
        uses: actions/cache@v4
        with:
          path: |
            ~/.cache/survtrend
            python/.hypothesis
          key: testdata-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('tests/reference/**') }}
          restore-keys: |
            testdata-${{ runner.os }}-

      - name: Install survtrend
        run: python -m pip install --no-deps -e ".[dev]"

      - name: Run pytest
        env:
          RUN_SLOW: ${{ github.event_name == 'schedule' || inputs.run-slow-tests }}
          COV_ARGS: ${{ matrix.coverage && '--cov=survtrend --cov-report=xml' || '' }}
        run: |
          extra_args=()
          if [[ "$RUN_SLOW" == "true" ]]; then
            extra_args+=(--runslow)
          fi
          pytest tests -n auto --durations=20 $COV_ARGS "${extra_args[@]}"

      - name: Upload coverage to Codecov
        if: matrix.coverage && github.repository == 'ecolab-uni/survtrend'
        uses: codecov/codecov-action@v5
        with:
          files: python/coverage.xml
          flags: python
          token: ${{ secrets.CODECOV_TOKEN }}
          fail_ci_if_error: false

  reference-results:
    # Both implementations must reproduce the shared reference results.
    needs: [R-CMD-check, pytest]
    if: github.event_name != 'schedule'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: r-lib/actions/setup-r@v2
        with:
          use-public-rspm: true

      - uses: r-lib/actions/setup-r-dependencies@v2
        with:
          working-directory: r
          extra-packages: local::.

      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: "3.12"
          cache: pip
          cache-dependency-path: python/pyproject.toml

      - name: Compare R and Python results
        run: |
          python -m pip install ./python
          make -C tests/reference compare TOLERANCE=1e-6

# Kubernetes manifests for the survtrend Shiny dashboard and the lab's
# JupyterHub user profiles. Apply with:
#
#   kubectl apply -f kubernetes_multi_document.yaml
#
# The cluster runs ingress-nginx and cert-manager. JupyterHub itself is
# installed with the zero-to-jupyterhub Helm chart (infra/jupyterhub/values.yaml).
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: shiny-server-config
  namespace: ecolab-apps
data:
  shiny-server.conf: |
    # Run applications as the unprivileged "shiny" user
    run_as shiny;
    preserve_logs true;
    sanitize_errors true;

    server {
      listen 3838;

      location / {
        site_dir /srv/shiny-server/survtrend-dashboard;
        log_dir /var/log/shiny-server;
        directory_index off;
        app_idle_timeout 600;
        app_init_timeout 120;
      }
    }
  DASHBOARD_TITLE: "Grassland insect monitoring – survtrend dashboard"
  API_BASE_URL: "http://survey-api.ecolab-apps.svc.cluster.local:8000/v1"
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: dashboard-db-credentials
  namespace: ecolab-apps
type: Opaque
stringData:
  PGHOST: postgres.ecolab-data.svc.cluster.local
  PGDATABASE: surveys
  PGUSER: dashboard_ro
  # Placeholder only: the real value is managed by sealed-secrets.
  PGPASSWORD: "REPLACE_ME"
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
metadata:
  name: dashboard-cache
  namespace: ecolab-apps
spec:
  accessModes: [ReadWriteMany]
  storageClassName: nfs-client
  resources:
    requests:
      storage: 5Gi
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: survtrend-dashboard
  namespace: ecolab-apps
  labels: &dashboard-labels
    app.kubernetes.io/name: survtrend-dashboard
    app.kubernetes.io/component: shiny
    app.kubernetes.io/part-of: survtrend
  annotations:
    kubernetes.io/change-cause: "Update to survtrend 1.3.0 for the autumn 2026 monitoring report"
spec:
  replicas: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels: *dashboard-labels
  strategy:
    type: RollingUpdate
    rollingUpdate: {maxSurge: 1, maxUnavailable: 0}
  template:
    metadata:
      labels: *dashboard-labels
    spec:
      securityContext:
        runAsUser: 999
        runAsGroup: 999
        fsGroup: 999
      containers:
        - name: shiny
          image: ghcr.io/ecolab-uni/survtrend-dashboard:1.3.0
          imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent
          ports:
            - name: http
              containerPort: 3838
          envFrom:
            - secretRef:
                name: dashboard-db-credentials
          env:
            - name: DASHBOARD_TITLE
              valueFrom:
                configMapKeyRef: {name: shiny-server-config, key: DASHBOARD_TITLE}
            - name: API_BASE_URL
              valueFrom:
                configMapKeyRef: {name: shiny-server-config, key: API_BASE_URL}
            - name: R_CONFIG_ACTIVE
              value: production
          resources:
            requests: {cpu: 250m, memory: 512Mi}
            limits: {cpu: "1", memory: 2Gi}
          readinessProbe:
            httpGet: {path: /, port: http}
            initialDelaySeconds: 15
            periodSeconds: 10
          livenessProbe:
            httpGet: {path: /, port: http}
            initialDelaySeconds: 60
            periodSeconds: 30
            failureThreshold: 3
          volumeMounts:
            - name: config
              mountPath: /etc/shiny-server/shiny-server.conf
              subPath: shiny-server.conf
            - name: cache
              mountPath: /srv/cache
      volumes:
        - name: config
          configMap:
            name: shiny-server-config
        - name: cache
          persistentVolumeClaim:
            claimName: dashboard-cache
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: survtrend-dashboard
  namespace: ecolab-apps
spec:
  selector:
    app.kubernetes.io/name: survtrend-dashboard
    app.kubernetes.io/component: shiny
  ports:
    - name: http
      port: 80
      targetPort: http
---
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: Ingress
metadata:
  name: survtrend-dashboard
  namespace: ecolab-apps
  annotations:
    cert-manager.io/cluster-issuer: letsencrypt-prod
    # Shiny keeps per-session state in the R process, so all requests of a
    # session must reach the same pod (sticky sessions via a cookie).
    nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/affinity: cookie
    nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/session-cookie-name: shiny-route
    nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/session-cookie-max-age: "28800"
    nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/proxy-read-timeout: "3600"
    nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/proxy-send-timeout: "3600"
spec:
  ingressClassName: nginx
  tls:
    - hosts: [dashboard.ecolab.example.edu]
      secretName: dashboard-tls
  rules:
    - host: dashboard.ecolab.example.edu
      http:
        paths:
          - path: /
            pathType: Prefix
            backend:
              service:
                name: survtrend-dashboard
                port:
                  name: http
---
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: CronJob
metadata:
  name: refresh-trend-cache
  namespace: ecolab-apps
spec:
  # Refit the site-level trends every night so that the dashboard opens quickly.
  schedule: "30 2 * * *"
  timeZone: Europe/Berlin
  concurrencyPolicy: Forbid
  jobTemplate:
    spec:
      backoffLimit: 2
      template:
        spec:
          restartPolicy: OnFailure
          containers:
            - name: refresh
              image: ghcr.io/ecolab-uni/survtrend-dashboard:1.3.0
              command: ["Rscript", "-e"]
              args:
                - |
                  library(survtrend)
                  con <- DBI::dbConnect(RPostgres::Postgres())
                  surveys <- read_survey(con, table = "catches_harmonised")
                  fits <- fit_trend(surveys, by = "site_id", family = "tweedie")
                  saveRDS(fits, "/srv/cache/trend-fits.rds")
                  DBI::dbDisconnect(con)
              envFrom:
                - secretRef: {name: dashboard-db-credentials}
              volumeMounts:
                - {name: cache, mountPath: /srv/cache}
          volumes:
            - name: cache
              persistentVolumeClaim: {claimName: dashboard-cache}
---
# Extra single-user profiles for JupyterHub, mounted into the hub pod and
# loaded from hub.extraConfig in the Helm values.
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: jupyterhub-profiles
  namespace: ecolab-jupyter
data:
  profiles.yaml: |
    - display_name: "Python 3.12 (survtrend, 4 CPU / 16 GB)"
      slug: survtrend-py
      default: true
      kubespawner_override:
        image: ghcr.io/ecolab-uni/survtrend-notebook:2026.11
        cpu_limit: 4
        mem_limit: 16G
    - display_name: "R 4.4 with RStudio (2 CPU / 8 GB)"
      slug: rstudio
      kubespawner_override:
        image: rocker/binder:4.4.2
        default_url: /rstudio
        cpu_limit: 2
        mem_limit: 8G
